newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Arco wins Venezuelan Maulpa oil contract.
newsitem.headline: Arco wins Venezuelan Maulpa oil contract.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield (ARCO) in association with Venezuela's Inelectra and Polar Uno agreed Monday to pay $61.37 for the contract to operate Venezuela's Maulpa oil field, state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) said.

The consortium, which had already successfully bid $60 million for the Kaki field on Monday morning -- was among eight bidders on the first day of Venezuela's third round of oil operating contract auctions.

The field, discovered in 1957 in eastern Venezuela, currently produces 1,580 barrels per day (bpd) from two active wells and has proven reserves of 119 million barrels, according to PDVSA estimates. Ten other wells are inactive.

Under the 20-year contract, the operator will produce hydrocarbons on behalf of PDVSA subsidiary Corpoven in exchange for a fee worked out on a sliding scale. The operator must also invest at least $5 million within three years, although PDVSA expects investment to be higher.
The field was one of five reserved for consortia with at least 30 percent Venezuelan participation and is the highest producing of the five.
Contracts for three other fields have already been auctioned Monday including, apart from Kaki, Casma-Anaco for $27.58 million and Mata for $90.78 million.
A total of 131 companies are competing for 20 contracts to be sold this week with the winners determined purely by the size of their bids.
